text: The barguest is a shapeshifter from the folklore of Britain and Scotland. It is easily mixed up with bogies, boggarts, and brownies. In both England and Scotland the creature was reported for many years. It could shift into many bodies. One form shows a body with no head. Another looks like a pale phantom hare. A third takes the shape of a white cat. Most often the beast appeared as a black dog. That dark form tended to show when a respected local person lay dying. At those times its eyes blazed with flame and every dog in the district began to howl without stop. Meeting the barguest was a bad omen. A bite from it would never heal. Its name may come from the words for bear-ghost. It may also come from barrow-ghost. A barrow is an old grave mound. The barguest was said to roam such ancient burials.
